messages:
maria: Draft RFC for kernel-routing + SLA tradeoffs: https://redwood.in/rfc/kernel-routing
maria: TL;DR — change runtime to prefer low-latency kernels for p95-sensitive routes, fallback to cost-efficient kernels when queued; need acceptance criteria, rollout plan, and edge cases.
rahul: reading. can we add a deterministic tie-breaker when multiple kernels match? last-wins can be spooky.
jess: agree, deterministic order is must. also define perf reg thresholds: p95 token latency regression <= 5% vs baseline.
kevin: SRE question: how does this interact with cross-region failover? want explicit fallback policy to avoid cold-starting large kernels midflight.
sophie: customer ask: for Dedicated customers, they'd prefer pin-to-kernel option to guarantee bit-identical behavior. add acceptance criteria for 'pinned' mode.
rahul: noted. propose config snippet:
```
kernel_routing:
  priority: ["low_latency","balanced","cost"]
  tie_breaker: "stable_id"
  pinned_mode: false
```
maria: Nice. Acceptance criteria proposal:
- unit tests for selector logic
- perf bench: p50,p95,p99 token latency and throughput within +-5% of baseline for low-latency route
- canary rollout with 5% traffic for 48h
- KV cache hit-rate delta < 2% after rollout
jess: also add regression test for KV cache invalidation when model version bumps (we saw issues in last rollout).
kevin: monitoring: create SLOs and alerting:
- alert if p95 increases >15% over baseline for 15m
- alert if error-rate >0.5%
rahul: edge case: models with custom kernels (third-party) — should we allow forced bypass? maybe a sandbox flag.
maria: decision: add 'allow_custom_kernels' flag per org. Acceptance criteria: docs + e2e with private deploy.
sophie: can we add a customer scenario to PRD: "real-time chat with strict 300ms p95" and one for "batch embeddings cost-optimized"? helps prioritize.
maria: good — I'll append those to PRD.
kevin: rollout notes: feature flag + gradual concurrency ramps, verify KV cache warmup script runs on new kernels.
ops-bot: deploy scheduled: canary job queued for 2026-03-21 02:00 UTC — please ack.
rahul: ack. I'll start an implementation RFC and link tests. assign reviewers @jess @kevin @sophie
maria: thanks — please comment on the doc by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
